notes.claim: When the denominators are the same, you add the numerators; to subtract, subtract the numerators and the denominator remains the same.
Adding halves to halves is counting halves; adding fractions with different denominators needs one or both fractions changed so that they have the same denominator.
To add or subtract fractions that are not related, the product of the two denominators provides a common denominator.
Converting to equivalent fractions by multiplying top and bottom by the same number keeps the value of each fraction the same.

sources.title: Equivalent fractions (video) | Khan Academy
sources.quote: If I multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number, then I'm not changing what that fraction represents.

sources.title: Common denomination: more adding and subtracting | NCETM
sources.quote: To add and subtract non-related fractions, the product of the two denominators provides a common denominator.

sources.title: Common Denominator
sources.quote: We multiplied the top and bottom of each fraction by the denominator of the other: this keeps the value of the fraction the same!

sources.title: Common Denominator
sources.quote: Then we can add the top numbers and keep the denominator the same.

sources.title: Adding and subtracting fractions - BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: When the denominators are the same you can just add the numerators.

sources.title: Adding and subtracting fractions - BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: When you're adding and subtracting fractions with different denominators, you need to change one, and sometimes both, of the fractions so that they have the same denominator.

sources.title: How to subtract fractions - BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: To find the difference between fractions with the same denominator, subtract the numerators. The denominator remains the same.
